solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Endlessly carp? Coming round in the end

indicators.note: coming round says the shortened fish goes around the next word
endlessly says the word for carp loses its final letter

parts.note: a carp is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumbler is told their complaining will come round to something in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp?' looks like 'complain' but is the fish; the question mark flags it as an example. FIS goes round IN; 'Coming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin word printed at the close of a book or film, meaning conclusion.

clue.text: What keeps nurse going, perhaps German convenience food

parts.note: a nurse shark is a fish, and what keeps a fish going (swimming) is a fin

explanation.surface: Asks what keeps a nurse going through a shift, perhaps some German ready meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The nurse is a nurse shark, not a hospital worker; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded strips of white fish are a classic frozen ready-to-cook food.

clue.text: Censure over card game

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to pan a show is to censure it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised over the way they played cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple trick-taking game, short for Napoleon.

clue.text: Son gets rather mad covered in acne

parts.note: potty is British slang for slightly crazy

explanation.surface: A teenage son is driven half crazy by his spotty skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin dotted with pimples is described as blemished in this way.

clue.text: Complain luxury boat is unfinished, cutting beauty

indicators.note: cutting says the shortened boat slices into the word for beauty

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: is unfinished says the boat word loses its last letter

parts.note: a yacht is a luxury boat

explanation.surface: Someone moans that a half-built yacht is spoiling a lovely view.
explanation.walkthrough: YACH (YACHT without its last letter) cuts into BELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal verb for grumbling or whining at length.

clue.text: Wealthier gambler not going into work

parts.note: a better is one who bets
someone off is away from work

explanation.surface: A gambler who skips work ends up richer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for having more money or being in a more comfortable position.

clue.text: Slow and dignified film, but not indispensible

indicators.note: but not says one part of the film title is taken away

parts.note: Key Largo is a 1948 Bogart film
something indispensable is key

explanation.surface: A critic calls a film slow and stately, but hardly essential viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indispensible' is the clue's spelling of indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical tempo marking for a broad, stately pace.

clue.text: Conceding Yankee playing cricket has no following

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: has no says a letter is removed from the cricket word

parts.note: fielding is the job of the side not batting in cricket
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An American gives up on cricket because nobody follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving way or surrendering, as in a soldier giving ground.

clue.text: Pedestrian in public location

parts.note: common land is shared by the public
a place is a location

explanation.surface: A walker is out in a public place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker, but it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean ordinary, dull and unremarkable.

clue.text: Mostly ancient member of a noble line

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: early here means from long ago, primitive

explanation.surface: Describes an ancestor from long ago in an aristocratic family.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above viscount and below marquess.

clue.text: Champion drink, beer

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A winner celebrates with a drink of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a winner, but it is the sense of a backer or advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who champions a cause is a backer or advocate of it.

clue.text: Ecosystem merits having this wheat planted in it

indicators.note: planted in it says the word sits buried inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A conservation note praising an ecosystem for growing a certain grain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient cultivated grain species, ancestor of durum.

clue.text: Depart this earth — left to disappear as soon as possible

indicators.note: to disappear says that letter goes

parts.note: to depart this earth is to go from the world, phrased in inverted order

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave this world immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: Departing this earth is 'from the world go'; losing L turns WORLD into WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning from the very outset, right at once.

clue.text: Big loud unit relocated in separate housing

indicators.note: relocated says these letters move into new positions

explanation.surface: A big noisy unit has been moved to its own building.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed or barn standing apart from the main house.

clue.text: Hotels mounted very intense type of water sport

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel, so hotels are hydros

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted says the word climbs, reading upwards

parts.note: deep can mean very intense, as in deep sleep

explanation.surface: Hotels are promoting a very intense water sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding down white water on a float board, a sport also called riverboarding.

clue.text: Acquire small area for training bats?

parts.note: to net something is to acquire it

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a little space to train bats, the flying animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' means batsmen, so the definition is cricket practice; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket practice enclosures of netting where batsmen train.

clue.text: Hurry up — seems diaper is needed here

parts.note: looks means seems
nappy is the British word for diaper

explanation.surface: A parent is told to hurry, as a baby clearly needs changing.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom urging someone to be quick.

clue.text: Run home to look up family line

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word reads upwards

parts.note: to peek is to look
a house is a dynasty, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone hurries home to research their family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run home' looks like dashing back; it means manage a household.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a household's domestic affairs.

clue.text: Like an old civilisation rains, say, destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: An ancient civilisation is wiped out by rains, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the ancient Mesopotamian empire centred on Nineveh.

clue.text: I reuse film running in mixer

indicators.note: running says the letters are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recycles old film in a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent that blends oil and water, e.g. lecithin.

clue.text: One enters level two

indicators.note: enters says the letter goes inside the next word

parts.note: par means level, as in on a par
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum where one enters level two.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple or brace of things.

clue.text: Fear ferret I introduced to father

indicators.note: introduced to says these letters are put inside the word for father

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a hob is a male ferret

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of a ferret is introduced to their father.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrational dread, such as arachnophobia.

clue.text: "Cast in Chains" — song by The Wretches

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
heels are contemptible people, wretches

explanation.surface: Reads like a song title and band name: a track by The Wretches.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning to imprison or put in fetters.

clue.text: Fungus certainly turns up after vase is removed

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, certainly

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the remaining letters read upwards
is removed says the vase word is taken out

parts.note: an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A fungus surely appears once the vase is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing URN from 'turns' leaves TS, which turned up gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled fungus used to raise bread and brew beer.

clue.text: Playwright that's taken round for a staged production

indicators.note: taken round for a says a ring-shaped letter replaces an A

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw is the Irish playwright
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A playwright is shown round a theatre before a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical performance or entertainment on stage.

clue.text: Some island seized by Henry I

definitions.text: Some island seized by Henry I

indicators.note: seized by says the island word is held between the letters

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: Tells of a king capturing an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The nation occupies part of an island (Hispaniola), hence 'Some island'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean nation sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Outline provided by a stupid judge

parts.note: dumb means stupid
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A sketch supplied by a foolish judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or sketch in broad strokes.

clue.text: Difficulty of a year that never was

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks a year of the Christian era
zero, written O, stands for a year that did not exist

explanation.surface: Problems dating from a year that never existed.
explanation.walkthrough: There was no year AD 0: the calendar went from 1 BC to AD 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Carriage departed before time during endless floods, perhaps

indicators.note: during says these letters fall within the shortened water word
endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: floods are an example of water

indicators.note: before puts the departed word ahead of the time letter

parts.note: gone means departed

explanation.surface: A carriage left just before floods arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floods, perhaps' defines by example, and 'endless' trims it before the departed-plus-time letters go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn pleasure vehicle.

clue.text: Keen to eat old duck

indicators.note: to eat says the keen word swallows the letter

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to eat an old duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep or evade something.
